overview: This Senate resolution celebrates the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the international soccer tournament jointly hosted for the first time by three countries: the United States, Canada and Mexico. It notes the tournament's expanded format of 48 teams and 104 matches in 16 host cities, 11 of them in the United States. It welcomes fans and players, thanks Canada and Mexico for working together on hosting, recognizes the host cities, and supports sport as a way to bring people together. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on July 15, 2026.
for: Supporters say it welcomes visitors from around the world and recognizes a major event and partnership with neighboring countries.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
